dedupe_keys.name: unicef oxygen system planning tool ospt health facility oxygen demand source selection and costing

description: The Oxygen System Planning Tool is an Excel-based, customisable tool for planning medical oxygen delivery systems from source to patient, published by UNICEF. It estimates oxygen demand at each health facility from facility type, patient numbers and disease prevalence, groups facilities into archetypes to aggregate demand across an area or level of the health system, and recommends the most appropriate and cost-effective source for each facility, such as cylinders refilled from central plants, on-site pressure swing adsorption plants or concentrators. It calculates distances between facilities and known oxygen plants, supports placement of new PSA plants, produces procurement lists of equipment, consumables and diagnostics with replacement schedules, and estimates capital and operating costs, including electricity, aggregated by administrative level. Coverage is any country or region that supplies facility data; the Ghana Ministry of Health piloted it in the Eastern Region in 2020 to 2021. The tool, reference guide and introductory training are free from UNICEF, with a mailing list for updates. Caveats: results depend on the facility data and parameters users enter, it is a planning spreadsheet, not a network simulator, and power supply reliability is only reflected in costs. Simulation uses: sizing oxygen supply for health facilities, testing dependence of oxygen systems on electricity and transport, and costing resilience investments. Related records: the WHO Harmonized Health Facility Assessment (data-who-harmonized-health-facility-assessment-hhfa) provides facility readiness data and DHIS2 (platform-dhis2) holds routine health data.
